_description: Matt Pocock v1.1 development lifecycle as a Ringer swarm: grill → spec → tickets → implement → code-review. Each task uses Pocock skills as agent instructions.

tasks.spec: Load the /grilling skill (productivity/grilling/SKILL.md). Interview the user relentlessly about the project: {{PROJECT_DESCRIPTION}}. Ask ONE question at a time. Distinguish Facts (found by exploring) from Decisions (user must decide). Do not enact any plan until the user confirms shared understanding. Write the full grilling transcript and outcomes to ./grilling-output.md.
tasks.check: test -s grilling-output.md && grep -qiE 'decision|question|confirm' grilling-output.md && echo 'grilling OK'
tasks.verified: grilling-output.md exists, is non-empty, and records decisions/questions

tasks.spec: Load the /to-spec skill (engineering/to-spec/SKILL.md). Turn the grilling output (./grilling-output.md) into a spec. The spec defines the destination — where we're going with this feature or project. Quiz which modules we're touching. Write the spec to ./spec.md and publish to the issue tracker if configured.
tasks.check: test -s spec.md && grep -qiE 'module|spec|requirement' spec.md && echo 'to-spec OK'
tasks.verified: spec.md exists, is non-empty, and references modules/requirements

tasks.spec: Load the /to-tickets skill (engineering/to-tickets/SKILL.md). Break the spec (./spec.md) into tracer-bullet vertical slices — each ticket declaring its blocking edges. Write tickets to ./tickets.md (local file mode) or create them in the issue tracker if configured.
tasks.check: test -s tickets.md && grep -qiE 'ticket|block|depend' tickets.md && echo 'to-tickets OK'
tasks.verified: tickets.md exists, is non-empty, and references blocking/dependency edges

tasks.spec: Load the /implement skill (engineering/implement/SKILL.md) and /tdd skill (engineering/tdd/SKILL.md). Implement the first ticket from ./tickets.md. Use TDD where possible: Red (write failing test) → Green (make test pass). Run type checking regularly. Single test files regularly. Do not refactor during implementation — refactoring is handled in code review.
tasks.verified: implementation artifact exists and is non-empty

tasks.spec: Load the /code-review skill (engineering/code-review/SKILL.md). Review the implementation on two axes using parallel sub-agents: (1) Standards — does it follow coding standards? Check for Fowler refactoring smells: mysterious name, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, repeated switches, divergent change, speculative generality, message chains, middleman. (2) Spec — does it faithfully implement the originating ticket from ./tickets.md? Write review to ./code-review.md.
tasks.check: test -s code-review.md && grep -qiE 'standards|spec|smell|review' code-review.md && echo 'code-review OK'
tasks.verified: code-review.md exists, is non-empty, and covers both axes
